prompt:
Honest answer: you can't rebuild ElevenLabs. The voices are the product,
frontier TTS models plus cloning safety and licensing, and none of that is a
weekend of code.

What you can build is a personal TTS workbench wrapping models you can run:

- A Node CLI plus a small local web page (Express, localhost only): paste text,
  pick a voice preset, get an mp3.
- Engine 1: Piper or Kokoro running locally on CPU, decent quality, free,
  private. Engine 2: optional OpenAI TTS fallback, key in .env, for when
  quality beats privacy.
- Save every generation to ~/TTS/YYYY-MM-DD/<slug>.mp3 with a sidecar .txt of
  the input text plus the engine and voice used.
- Voice presets in voices.json: name, engine, voice id, speed.
- Batch mode: point it at a folder of .txt files, get a folder of mp3s, good
  for narrating notes or articles.
- No accounts, no telemetry, local-first; the only network calls are the
  optional hosted API.
- Out of scope: voice cloning, dubbing, emotional voice direction. Do not clone
  real people's voices, that is exactly the part that should not be DIY.
- README: model download steps and an honest note on the quality gap versus
  ElevenLabs.
